newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Foreign investment in Indonesia falls in Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Indonesia falls in Jan-May.

text.p: Indonesia approved foreign investment proposals amounting to $14.4 billion in the first five months of the year, a drop of 25.5 percent compared to the year-ago period, the Jakarta Post reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo as saying the drop was because of the country's general elections, held last month, and was not worrying.
"Foreign investment approvals in 1992 (the year of the previous general elections) dropped 40 percent compared to 1991 so there have been worse times," he was quoted as saying.
"This is a five-year cycle for us," he added. "It happens everywhere else in the world at election time. Businesses wait to see who will win and what will happen."
Sanyoto said the approved proposals did not include investments in the services, financial and oil and gas sectors.
He said also that foreign investments should increase toward the end of the third quarter, as had happened in the last election year.
The ruling Golkar party swept the May 29 general elections with an estimated 74 percent of the vote.
The minister added that during the 1989-1994 development plan period, Indonesia approved foreign investments worth $44 billion.
"But now -- in the fourth year of the current 1994-1999 plan -- we have already licensed $108 billion in new foreign investments," he was quoted as saying.
"This means that even if we have no additional foreign investment approvals, what we have achieved in this five-year development plan is twice as much as in the last."
